design_rationale: This was a parallel-arm randomized controlled trial using centrally generated computer random numbers to allocate 70 participants 1:1 to microperc or RIRS.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated centrally, concealed from the operating surgeon until immediately before the procedure, and measured baseline characteristics were reasonably balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Simple randomization was performed centrally using computer-generated random numbers. Randomization was revealed to the operating surgeon just before starting each procedure.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants and personnel were unblinded, both groups received the assigned procedures under otherwise similar care, all randomized patients were analyzed, and the few clinically necessary conversions or auxiliary procedures were transparently reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Neither patients nor the study authors were blinded to the procedure... All the patients were included in the final analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for all 70 randomized participants, including three-month stone-clearance results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: There were 35 patients in each group. All the patients were included in the final analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were measured similarly across groups with prespecified methods, but outcome assessors were unblinded and several outcomes, including pain and surgeon discomfort, were subjective and therefore susceptible to knowledge of treatment assignment; stone clearance by KUB was also less sensitive than CT.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Neither patients nor the study authors were blinded to the procedure... Clearance was defined as no residual stone on KUB at 3 months.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary and secondary outcomes are stated and reported, but no protocol, trial registration, or prespecified statistical analysis plan is provided to exclude selective choice among outcome measurements or analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary objective was to compare stone clearance rates and secondary objectives were to compare operating time, requirement for intra-operative JJ stenting, complications according to the Clavien–Dindo classification system, conversion to other procedures, surgeon discomfort score, haemoglobin drop, postoperative pain, analgesic requirement and hospital stay.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns. Randomization, allocation concealment, complete follow-up, and analysis were sound, but lack of blinding could influence subjective outcome measurement, and absence of a reported protocol or registration leaves some concern about selective reporting.

design_rationale: This was an explicitly randomized parallel-group trial using computer-generated random numbers, stratified by site, to allocate 160 patients 1:1 to SMP or RIRS.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was computer-generated and stratified by site, with broadly comparable baseline groups, but the report does not clearly establish that allocation was concealed from recruiters until each participant was irreversibly enrolled.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Parallel randomization was conducted at a ratio of 1:1, stratified by site and was carried out using computer-generated random numbers. The coordinating center revealed randomization to the operating surgeon at the time of surgical scheduling.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although participants and surgeons were unblinded and several clinically necessary postponements or conversions occurred, these were documented and the principal analysis followed intention-to-treat, reducing bias from deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The surgeons and patients were no blinded to group assignment... The analysis was done according to the intention-to-treat principle.

domain_judgments.rationale: The intention-to-treat results retain all 80 randomized participants in each group, and the reported 3-month stone-free counts use denominators of 80 per group, indicating outcome data were available or conservatively handled for essentially all randomized patients.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Final SFR at 3-month postoperatively... Intention-to-treat analysis... 75 (93.8) [SMP]... 66 (82.5) [RIRS].

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was objectively defined and assessed with the same imaging schedule in both groups by investigators blinded to the surgical procedure, making differential measurement unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Investigators who had not been involved and blinded to the surgical procedures performed the postoperative clinical assessment... Low-dose CT with a 2 mm section thickness was obtained for all patients at 3-months follow-up to evaluate the stone-free status.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and the primary endpoint and analysis approach are stated, but the supplied report does not provide the protocol or prespecified statistical analysis plan needed to exclude selective choice among time points, outcome definitions, or analyses, and it presents both intention-to-treat and per-protocol results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial was registered at http://clinicaltrials.gov/ (NCT02519634)... We also did a per-protocol analysis of the primary endpoints.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged some concerns, driven by incomplete reporting of allocation concealment and insufficient information to rule out selective reporting despite prospective registration. The objective, blinded outcome assessment, complete ITT denominators, and appropriate ITT analysis otherwise support low risk in the remaining domains.

design_rationale: The Methods explicitly state that allocation to UMPNL or RIRS was determined by tossing a coin.

domain_judgments.rationale: A random coin-toss sequence was reported, but allocation concealment was not described and the clinically important stone-location distribution was significantly imbalanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization for UMPNL or RIRS procedures was done with tossing a coin method... The groups were different for localizations of the stones (p=0.020).

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding was not reported and each intervention was delivered by a different surgeon, while no intention-to-treat analysis or information about crossover and protocol deviations was provided.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: one surgeon performed UMPNL, and another performed RIRS. Both are highly experienced surgeons.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome results were reported for all 73 randomized participants, with group totals consistently remaining 30 and 43 and no attrition indicated.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 73 patients with stone sizes of 10-25 mm, and had RIRS or UMPNL procedures were included in the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Stone-free status was measured objectively and consistently by CT, but assessor blinding was not reported, and subjective outcomes such as pain and return to normal life were vulnerable to knowledge of treatment assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Postoperative pain was determined by visual analog scale (VAS), asked by the same physician to all patients 2 hours after surgery... Stone-free status was determined with low-dose non-contrast CT obtained one month after surgery.

domain_judgments.rationale: No prespecified protocol or analysis plan was reported, and multiple outcomes and unplanned-looking stone-location subgroup analyses were available; the highlighted lower-pole finding is especially vulnerable because baseline stone location differed significantly between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Therefore, we analyzed our stone-free rates in UMPNL and RIRS procedures in relation with the localizations of the stones... The limitation of our study is difference in the distribution of the localizations of the stones in two groups.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by high risk of selective reporting from numerous outcomes and subgroup analyses without reported prespecification, particularly the emphasized lower-pole result amid a significant baseline imbalance in stone location. Additional concerns include unreported allocation concealment, lack of blinding, surgeon-treatment confounding, and no stated intention-to-treat analysis.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports 1:1 parallel randomization using computer-generated random numbers in Stata.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-generated random sequence and balanced baseline characteristics were reported, but concealment of allocation until assignment was not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Simple random sampling was adopted, and parallel randomization was conducted at a ratio of 1:1, stratified by site, and was carried out using computer software STATA version 13.0 ... to generate random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was unblinded, four MPCNL procedures were aborted after allocation, and reported analyses excluded these participants rather than clearly applying intention-to-treat, although the abortions appear clinically indicated.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Four patients assigned in the MPCNL group had purulent fluid in the initial puncture, and the following MPCNL procedure was aborted.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome tables include all 110 FURL participants but only 106 of 110 assigned to MPCNL after four procedures were aborted, and no analysis establishing that this post-randomization exclusion could not bias outcomes was reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: FIG. 2. ... n = 110 for FURL group, n = 106 for MPCNL group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were defined and assessed on common schedules, but the study was unblinded and assessor blinding was not reported, creating potential influence on subjective pain/comfort scores and discharge timing even though imaging and laboratory outcomes were more objective.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A prospective, simple random sampling and unblinded controlled study were performed from May 2017 to July 2019 at Peking University Shougang Hospital.

domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol or preregistration is reported, and numerous outcomes, repeated time points, and alternative statistical analyses leave scope for selective reporting despite presentation of many measured results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Categoric data were analyzed using the Chi-square test. Continuous variable was assessed with t-test or post hoc test for the two-way analysis of variance analysis.

overall_summary: The trial has some concerns overall because allocation concealment was not reported, four participants assigned to MPCNL were excluded from outcome analyses, and the unblinded design could affect subjective outcomes and discharge decisions. Lack of a reported protocol or preregistration also leaves scope for selective reporting.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that 70 enrolled patients were randomized 1:1 to mini-PCNL or RIRS, with randomization carried out by the institution's Department of Biostatistics.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was performed independently and apparently concealed until admission, but the sequence-generation method was not reported and notable baseline imbalances in hydronephrosis and stone complexity raise some concern, although they may reflect chance in this small trial.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was carried out by the Department of Biostatistics of our institution and opened to the operating surgeon at the time of the patient’s admission on the day before surgery.

domain_judgments.rationale: Two RIRS-assigned patients crossed over to mini-PCNL because of an allocation error and were excluded rather than analyzed in their randomized groups, so the analysis was not intention-to-treat and could be biased by post-randomization deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Two patients from the RIRS group received mini-PCNL because of the allocation error and dropped out of the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary-outcome data were available for 68 of 70 randomized patients, but both missing participants were from the RIRS arm and were excluded after receiving the other intervention, with no analysis showing that their missing outcomes could not bias the result.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 70 randomized patients, 68 completed the study including mini-PCNL in 35 and RIRS in 33.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary stone-free outcome was objectively measured by the same CT-based definition and time window in both groups, making assessor knowledge unlikely to materially influence measurement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Stone-free status was defined as no residual stones or stones <2 mm on NECT within 3 months postoperatively.

domain_judgments.rationale: A trial registration and prespecified primary endpoint are reported, but the manuscript does not provide enough information to verify prospective registration or a prespecified analysis plan, and numerous secondary outcomes and analyses create some potential for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This prospective randomized controlled trial (NCT02067221) aimed to compare mini-PCNL and RIRS for renal stones >10 mm.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because two participants assigned to RIRS received mini-PCNL and were excluded rather than analyzed according to randomized assignment. Additional concerns arise from incompletely described sequence generation, baseline imbalances, and limited information about prespecified analyses.

design_rationale: The study explicitly states that patients were allocated 1:1 to RIRS or PNL using an online research randomizer.

domain_judgments.rationale: A random sequence generator was used, but allocation concealment was not described and important baseline stone characteristics differed substantially between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After receiving patients’ written informed consent, the patients were randomized into either the RIRS group (Group 1) or PNL group (Group 2) in a ratio of 1:1 by using an online research randomizer (Fig. 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding was not reported and the procedures were readily distinguishable, while the unexplained reduction from 132 enrolled to 100 analyzed and absence of an explicit intention-to-treat analysis create concern about analysis according to assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 132 patients who suffered from renal stones, 2–4 cm in size, and had surgery at our urology clinic between April 2015 and April 2017 were enrolled in this prospective study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 100 of 132 enrolled participants appear in the analyzed groups, with no textual accounting for the 32 excluded or missing participants by randomized arm or reason, so outcome missingness could plausibly bias the results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: RIRS (n = 50) [and] PNL (n = 50)

domain_judgments.rationale: Pain was self-reported using an appropriate VAS at common time points, but participants could not plausibly be blinded to markedly different procedures and knowledge of treatment could influence this subjective outcome; blinding of analgesic administration was also not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients who were included in the study were asked to fill out a visual analog scale (VAS) questionnaire at 8 and 24 hours postoperatively.

domain_judgments.rationale: A trial registration number is provided, but the text does not establish that registration or a prespecified analysis plan preceded enrollment, and multiple pain time points and outcomes were analyzed without enough information to exclude selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The national clinical trial number of our study is NCT02430168 and Institutional Review Board number is IRB18-14.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high because 32 of 132 enrolled participants are not accounted for in the analyzed sample and the primary subjective pain outcome could have been influenced by participants' knowledge of the visibly different procedures. Additional concerns arise from unreported allocation concealment, baseline stone imbalances, and incomplete information about prespecified analyses.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports 1:1 allocation using computer-generated random numbers.

domain_judgments.rationale: The sequence was computer-generated and baseline characteristics were similar, but allocation concealment until irrevocable enrollment was not adequately described and the allocation was opened to the surgeon before surgery.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All enrolled patients were randomized to mPNL group and RIRS group with allocation 1:1. The randomization was carried out using computer-generated random numbers and opened to the operating surgeon before surgery.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding of patients and surgeons was infeasible and not reported, and the primary analysis excluded five randomized participants rather than clearly using intention-to-treat, although no intervention-related deviations were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eventually, 5 patients withdrew during the treatment and follow-up phase, with 115 patients enrolled in the primary outcome analysis (58 in the mPNL group and 57 in the RIRS group).

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome data were available for 115 of 120 randomized participants (95.8%), but reasons for the five withdrawals and evidence that missingness was unrelated to outcome were not provided.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Eventually, 5 patients withdrew during the treatment and follow-up phase, with 115 patients enrolled in the primary outcome analysis (58 in the mPNL group and 57 in the RIRS group).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was objectively measured by CT at the same three-month time point in both groups using a prespecified definition, and postoperative assessors were blinded to assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The postoperative assessment was performed by investigators who were unaware of the patients’ group assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and the primary outcome and time point were specified, but the provided report does not compare the published analyses against the registry/protocol or provide a prespecified statistical analysis plan sufficient to exclude selective analysis reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Besides, this study was prospectively registered at http:// www.chictr.org.cn (ChiCTR1800016983).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is some concerns. Although outcome assessment was objective and blinded, allocation concealment was insufficiently described, five randomized participants were excluded without reasons or intention-to-treat analysis, and selective reporting could not be fully excluded.
